mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by > 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances where GDPC1 dropped by > 1% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increased by > 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the last two months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increased by > 2% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer-driven sectors outperform.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio is above its historical median.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending decline.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases > 0.3% and PAYEMS decreases > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increased by > 0.3% and PAYEMS decreased by > 100k in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% during a monetary easing cycle signals accommodative policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate further easing.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 2% during an easing cycle.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of rising housing starts (HOUST) and increasing consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary pressure and strong demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as inflation-sensitive sectors outperform.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST increased by > 5% and CPIAUCSL increased by > 0.5% in the last month.
